goldQuery: how does highway select the best available SIMD target on first call and update the dispatch table
goldNotes: NL behavior probe. FunctionCache<RetType, Args...>::ChooseAndCall is the first-entry in every HWY_EXPORT table; it calls ChosenTarget::Update(SupportedTargets()) and then re-dispatches. This is the mechanism that makes the first HWY_DYNAMIC_DISPATCH invocation pay the detection cost while subsequent calls are a direct indexed function-pointer call. Tests chunking of a template struct with multiple member function templates inside the global hwy namespace.

Extension methods will fold into the surrounding file chunk rather than emit a named boundary. This probe is an honest grammar-edge-case marker; a PASS here would indicate the embedding model found the right file via header bigrams or surrounding context, not via a chunk-level entity match.

goldQuery: how does Penlight implement class inheritance with constructors and base method dispatch
goldNotes: NL behavior probe: `local function _class(base,c_arg,c)` (line 128) is Penlight's internal class factory — installs `_init` constructor, `is_a`/`class_of`/`cast` introspection, `super` for base method calls. The public `class` module (line 215-216, `class = setmetatable({}, ...)`) wraps `_class` as a callable. The chunker emits `_class` as the function chunk; `class` itself is an assigned-table (not function), so doesn't get its own entity.

goldQuery: how does highway track which SIMD target was chosen and return the index into the dispatch table
goldNotes: NL behavior probe. ChosenTarget is a monostate that stores an atomic int64_t bitmask and exposes GetIndex() (counts trailing zero bits to find the table slot), Update(), DeInit(), and IsInitialized(). Tests parser handling of a struct with conditional compilation: the mask_ field is std::atomic<int64_t> under libcxx but a plain int64_t under HWY_NO_LIBCXX, creating a bifurcated member declaration inside the struct body.
